title: Tylenol not linked to autism, new study shows, contradicting Trump administration claims
summary: A review of studies published in The Lancet found no link between acetaminophen use during pregnancy and autism, contradicting the Trump administration's recent claims.

title: Doctor on challenges in public health and impact: "The biggest problem is the confusion"
summary: Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel is an oncologist, professor and helped to write the Affordable Care Act. He speaks to "CBS Mornings" about confusion over changes to public health guidelines, living a fulfilling life and his new book, "Eat Your Ice Cream: Six Simple Rules for a Long and Healthy Life.

title: Nurses strike begins in New York City as thousands walk off jobs
summary: The largest nurses strike ever in New York City is underway as thousands of NYSNA members walk off their jobs at major hospitals.

title: NYC nurses strike looms as negotiations pass midnight deadline
summary: The potential for a major nurses strike in New York City is growing by the minute, with major hospitals and the New York State Nurses Association failing to get a deal done before Sunday's midnight deadline.

title: "Enough": Oprah Winfrey on her weight-loss lessons
summary: Oprah Winfrey is one of the best-known, most-admired and successful people on the planet. But for years she seemed powerless to conquer her fluctuating weight problem … until new medications, and a new attitude about her weight, gave her a breakthrough, which she describes in "Enough," a new book she has co-written with Dr. Ania Jastreboff. They talk with J…

title: State of denial: How insurance companies impact health care today
summary: As millions of Americans struggle with paying for health care, doctors and health experts discuss how medical care is being eroded by insurers denying necessary tests and treatment, making it "more difficult to be healthy in the United States."

title: Book excerpt: "Enough" by Dr. Ania Jastreboff and Oprah Winfrey
summary: The media superstar, who has struggled with weight for much of her life, and a Yale School of Medicine doctor team up for a book that examines the biology of obesity, offering a new way forward.

title: Potential health concerns with drinking water on some airlines, study finds
summary: A new study found potential health concerns with the drinking water on some airlines where you might order coffee or tea. The review was of airplane drinking water stored in onboard tanks, not bottled products. Of the 10 major airlines, Delta scored best, while JetBlue and American were the bottom two carriers.

title: Flu cases surge across U.S. as 45 states report "high or very high" virus activity
summary: There have been at least 11 million cases of the flu so far this season. As cases climb, doctor visits for the flu have hit their highest level in almost three decades, the CDC says. Skyler Henry reports.

title: CDC suggests fewer shots for kids in new vaccine recommendations
summary: The Trump administration is reducing the number of vaccines it recommends for children in the U.S. Under the new guidelines, the CDC recommends all children be vaccinated against 11 diseases, which is down from 17 immunizations. CBS News medical contributor Dr. Celine Gounder explains what to know.

title: Doctor's orders: Eat ice cream, and other tips for a long and healthy life
summary: In his new wellness book, "Eat Your Ice Cream," Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel goes beyond the basics of eating, exercise and sleep, to the importance of being happy, social engagement, and recommended behaviors (like "don't be a schmuck") that can benefit longevity.

title: Doctor's orders: Eat ice cream, and other tips for a long and healthy life
summary: In his new wellness book, "Eat Your Ice Cream: Six Simple Rules For a Long and Healthy Life," Dr. Ezekiel Emanuel, a prominent oncologist and health policy expert, goes beyond the basics of eating, exercise and sleep. He talks with Norah O'Donnell about the importance of being happy, social engagement, and recommended behaviors (like "don't be a schmuck") t…

title: Book excerpt: "Eat Your Ice Cream" by Ezekiel J. Emanuel, M.D.
summary: In his new book, the oncologist and health policy expert discusses longevity, and how to best differentiate valid and effective health and wellness advice from "the speculative, deceptive, and just plain stupid."

title: 18 states set to ban SNAP recipients from using benefits for some junk food in 2026
summary: In 2026, several states are set to prohibit individuals from purchasing certain junk food items using their federal benefits. Meg Oliver has the details.

title: New California tortilla law aims to decrease birth defects in Latino babies
summary: Mom-and-pop shops will be exempt from this change, but big manufacturers in California will need to start adding folic acid to tortillas beginning January 1.

title: New California tortilla law aims to decrease birth defects in Latino babies
summary: Mom-and-pop shops will be exempt from this change, but big manufacturers in California will need to start adding folic acid to tortillas beginning January 1.

title: Advances in treatment in the fight against Alzheimer's disease
summary: The number of Americans with Alzheimer's disease is expected to double from 7 million in 2020 to 14 million by 2060, according to the CDC. However, advances in treatment options are giving more people hope in slowing the decline. Dr. Jon LaPook breaks it down.

title: Flu cases skyrocket across the U.S.
summary: Nearly five million flu cases have been reported nationwide, the CDC estimates, and at least 1,900 people have died from the virus. "CBS Saturday Morning" has more on why this year's strain is breaking records.

title: Ovarian cancer survivor on finding hope through cancer clinical trials
summary: #LillyPartner Cancer clinical trials can offer patients access to investigational treatments that can be explored as early as the time of diagnosis. Ovarian cancer survivor Alicia Dellario and Dr. Arjun Balar, senior vice president of global clinical development at Eli Lilly and Company, join "CBS Mornings" to talk about the potential benefits of cancer cli…

title: What to know about the new flu strain as cases rise
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention estimates there have been 4.6 million flu cases across the U.S. since the season began. Dr. Amanda Kravitz, a pediatrician at Weill Cornell in New York, explains what to know about rising cases, symptoms to watch for and how to protect your family.

title: Flu cases surging nationwide
summary: Flu cases are on the rise across the country with CDC data showing more than 4 million illnesses this season resulting in roughly 2,000 deaths, including two children. Dr. Benjamin Abella, chair of emergency medicine at the Mount Sinai Health System in New York City, joined CBS News to discuss.

title: California warns against foraging mushrooms after cluster of poisonings, 1 death
summary: California's public health department said one person has died and several others have suffered severe liver damage due to eating toxic mushrooms that were foraged.

title: Millions of Americans could see health plan costs double as ACA credits vanish
summary: "I don't know how I'm going to pay for this," said one person with an Affordable Care Act plan that will cost her $1,100 a month starting in January.

title: Extended interview: Former CDC director Dr. Rochelle Walensky on hepatitis B vaccine
summary: CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook speaks at length with former CDC director Dr. Rochelle Walensky about the hepatitis B vaccine and last week's vote by the CDC's vaccine advisory panel to change the recommendation for when children should get their first dose of the vaccine.

title: Nuts sold at Wegmans stores in 9 states recalled over salmonella risk
summary: Mixed nuts from Ohio-based Mellace Family Brands sold at some Wegmans stores could be tainted with Salmonella, FDA warns.

title: How the CDC's decision on the hepatitis B vaccine at birth could impact infants
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's vaccine advisory panel on Friday voted to not recommend the hepatitis B vaccine for everyone at birth, alarming many in the medical community. CBS News medical contributor Dr. Celine Gounder explains what to know about the decision and its potential impact.

title: CEO of genetics firm says parents have a right to choose unborn child's traits
summary: Kian Sadeghi, the 25-year-old founder and CEO at Nucleus Genomics, tells "CBS Mornings" that parents have every right to select the qualities and traits they desire in their child.

title: How to avoid holiday stress
summary: The holiday season can be a wonderful, but also stressful time – filled with unrealistic expectations. A recent poll found 41% of adults anticipate more holiday stress this year. Psychiatrist Dr. Sue Varma has tips to unwind during the holidays.

title: San Francisco sues ultra-processed food makers
summary: In San Francisco on Tuesday, city attorney David Chiu announced the first government lawsuit of its kind against 11 companies that manufacture ultra-processed foods. Elizabeth Cook reports.

title: These 19 cooking pans could leach lead into your food, FDA warns
summary: Consumers with the imported pans should throw them away due to the severe health risks posed by lead, the agency warns.

title: Doctor who criticized vaccines named CDC principal deputy director
summary: Louisiana Surgeon General Ralph Abraham, a critic of government vaccine mandates, has been quietly appointed to one of the CDC's top positions.

title: How Medicare's lower prices for 15 medications could impact your costs
summary: The Trump administration tapped a Biden-era rule to negotiate lower prices on 15 widely used medications for seniors.

title: ClassPass founder's company reimagines classical Indian dance and helps young moms find community
summary: Payal Kadakia was just 27 when she came up with the idea for the popular app ClassPass, but it wasn't her first time building something from the ground up. In 2008, she created a dance company that reimagines classical Indian dance for a modern American audience.

title: ByHeart says all its baby formula could be tainted with botulism
summary: ByHeart said it can't rule out that all of its baby formula across all product lots could be contaminated, citing recent test results.

title: Doctor discusses cancer diagnosis for JFK's granddaughter, Tatiana Schlossberg
summary: This weekend, 35-year-old Tatiana Schlossberg, a granddaughter of former President John F. Kennedy, announced she has terminal cancer. CBS News medical contributor Dr. Celine Gounder has a breakdown of the diagnosis.

title: Powering our appetite for protein
summary: Proteins, whether from whey, plants or animals, are essential for building muscle. Last year, approximately 71% of consumers identified protein as the nutrient they most frequently try to eat. That's an appetite corporate America is more than happy to feed – even though protein often doesn't taste very good. Lee Cowan looks at how companies like General Mil…

title: Death in N.J. believed to be 1st linked to meat allergy spread by ticks
summary: A New Jersey man is the first person believed to have died from alpha-gal syndrome, a meat allergy triggered by a tick bite, researchers say.

title: Marjorie Taylor Greene says "I don't see political party lines" on health care
summary: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries called GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene an ally during the shutdown for joining Democrats in demanding that Congress address high health care costs.

title: New FDA-approved eye drop aims to help adults with age-related vision issues
summary: The once-daily, prescription eye drop is said to help combat presbyopia.

title: Air pollution in India's capital draws protests as schools are shuttered
summary: India's capital Delhi is blanketed in toxic smog every autumn, but the pollution is already so bad that it's drawn protests as authorities tell students to stay home.

title: Extended interview: FDA chief calls warnings on menopause treatments an "American tragedy"
summary: FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary tells CBS News' Norah O'Donnell in an exclusive interview why the agency decided to drop decades-old "black box" warnings on many hormone therapy drugs used for menopause and perimenopause symptoms.

title: FDA chief says warning labels deterred menopause care: "It's an American tragedy"
summary: In an interview with CBS News, FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary explains what went into the decision to drop the most serious warnings on hormone therapy for menopause.

title: Baby formula recalled as CDC investigates cases of infant botulism
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is investigating more than a dozen cases of infant botulism tied to the formula brand ByHeart, prompting a voluntary recall of the product. Officials say there have been 13 cases across 10 states since August. No deaths have been reported.

title: FDA chief explains changes to "black box" warnings on some hormone therapies for menopause
summary: FDA commissioner Dr. Marty Makary joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss the agency's announcement Thursday that boxed warnings will be removed from many estrogen products used for hormone therapy, a treatment that helps alleviate the symptoms of menopause.

title: Book excerpt: "The Day After Yesterday: Resilience in the Face of Dementia"
summary: Photographer Joe Wallace has chronicled the stories of families who have lived with Alzheimer's.
